hero.subtitle: Empowering children, teachers and mothers in Uganda through creativity, craftsmanship and practical skills.

about.label: Who We Are
about.heading: A small team with a big heart
paragraphs: After a private visit to the children's home with her family in the summer of 2024, Marcella L. had an idea: to open up space for creative thinking and hands-on making. Andreas S. and Anne S. later joined her — together we believe that creativity and practical skills can transform lives. In partnership with **Hands for an African Child (HFAAC)** in Bukomero, Uganda, we run hands-on crafting and skills programs first and foremost for the orphaned children of HFAAC — while their teachers and parents grow right alongside them, learning new skills of their own along the way.

Our first volunteers arrived in February 2025. Since then, 15 volunteers have taught on-site for a combined ten weeks, and we've helped hire and train seven local trainers who now run five ongoing programs every week during term time — computer skills, tailoring, carpentry, crafting classes and motorbike riding & maintenance. We're already back for our second intensive course in July 2026.
We are not a large NGO. We are people who show up, roll up their sleeves and craft something meaningful — together with the community.

programs.label: What We've Built
programs.heading: Five programs, running every week
programs.intro: What started as short volunteer visits has grown into five ongoing programs at Nuri Primary School — each one now carried forward by a local trainer, week after week, term after term.

items.title: 💻 Computer Lab
items.text: Four laptops, a laser printer and a SIM-based internet hub — set up by Andy, Heinz and Jari, now being run week to week by three local trainers preparing for ICDL-equivalent certification. Children learn word processing, spreadsheets, presentations and internet safety.
items.detailText: Four laptops, a laser printer and a SIM-based internet hub, teaching basic computer use, word processing, spreadsheets, presentations and internet safety. Three local trainers are being prepared to teach independently, with an eye toward ICDL-equivalent certification down the line.

items.title: 🪡 Tailoring Workshop
items.text: Sewing machines arrived at HFAAC for the first time in 2026, taught by Astrid, an experienced seamstress — students make reusable menstrual pads and skirts. Hand sewing is taught alongside, so there's always a way to sew, machine or not. Christine, our local trainer, now continues the lessons every week.
items.detailText: Astrid — an experienced seamstress — together with Anne and Marcella taught machine sewing for the very first time at HFAAC, focused on reusable menstrual pads and many, many skirts. Alongside the machines, hand sewing techniques are also taught, so students have both skills whether or not a machine is free. Christine, our local trainer, now continues the lessons every week.

items.title: 🪵 Carpentry Course
items.text: Using a mitre box saw, jigsaw, drill and pyrography pen, students measure, saw, sand and decorate their own wood pieces — Mölkky games, keychains, cutting boards and ABC learning blocks. Patrick, a foster father at HFAAC with a natural talent for woodwork, has led every session since 2025.
items.detailText: Building on 2025's basics — Mölkky games, keychains, cutting boards and ABC learning blocks — students tackle more complex wood projects with a manual mitre box saw, cordless jigsaw, drill and pyrography pen, refining measuring, sawing and finishing skills.

items.title: 🧶 Crafting Classes
items.text: Regular crafting classes run right in school — door mats, felt crowns, handmade dolls, bags, jewelry, toys and clothing — combining crochet and hand sewing. Anne and Audrey introduced more advanced stitches and patterns in 2026, building on what Esther and Filder already teach every week.
items.detailText: Led by Anne and Audrey, students built on their existing skills with more advanced stitches and patterns — making bags, jewelry, toys and clothing. Materials were partly sourced through a Relief Society service project collecting yarn and fabric back home. A few examples of what can be made, plus photos from on-site sessions:

items.title: 🏍️ Motorbike Riding & Maintenance
items.text: Safe Boda Boda handling, basic driving practice, road safety and simple maintenance like tyre and oil checks — led by Jari, and now continued week to week by Philip, our local trainer and caretaker of the motorbike.
items.detailText: Led by Jari together with local trainer Philip, students learned safe Boda Boda handling, basic driving practice, road safety and simple maintenance like tyre and oil checks. Philip now continues as the local trainer and caretaker of the motorbike.

items.title: Hannah & Emily — our first volunteers
items.text: The project kicks off! Over six weeks, Hannah and Emily work with the children on bracelets, carved figures, sewn pillows, clay, mobiles — and bake a lot of cookies together. They lay the groundwork for everything that follows.

items.title: Teacher Esther starts teaching textiles
items.text: Our first local craft teacher joins. Esther specializes in traditional techniques like weaving baskets and mats from banana fibre, and begins regular textile lessons with the children.

items.title: Teacher Filder joins — Boris, Sarah & Laura visit
items.text: Teacher Filder starts teaching textile work in July. In August, volunteers Boris, Sarah and Laura spend 2.5 weeks on-site, explore the local market, buy the first jigsaws and drills, and connect with Patrick, a foster father at HFAAC with a real talent for woodwork — expanding the program into technical crafts.

whatsNext.label: What's Next
whatsNext.heading: Connecting HFAAC
whatsNext.paragraph: Our next project is already in the pipeline: bringing internet to the entire HFAAC compound — from the medical center and community building to the teacher homes, office buildings and all the way up to the family homes. We'll start with a microwave data link over a fibre (glasfibre) connection with WiFi access points across the site, and switch to Starlink once it becomes available in the area.
whatsNext.thanksNote: A huge thank you to **Terry** from the US, who is generously supporting this project — and who will help bring Starlink to HFAAC once it's available in the area.

tags.label: 📡 Microwave Data Link
tags.detail: A wireless microwave data link will bring broadband to the HFAAC compound as the first step of the rollout.

tags.label: 🌐 Fibre Connection
tags.detail: A fibre (glasfibre) backbone connects the core buildings for fast, stable internet across the site.

tags.label: 📶 WiFi Access Points
tags.detail: WiFi access points spread the connection across the whole compound — from the medical center to the family homes.

tags.label: 🛰️ Starlink (future upgrade)
tags.detail: Once available in the area, the connection will be upgraded to Starlink satellite internet for even better speed and reliability.

tags.label: 🏥 Medical Center
tags.detail: Reliable internet will support the medical center's record-keeping and communication with outside doctors and specialists.

tags.label: 🏠 Family Homes
tags.detail: The rollout reaches all the way up to the family homes — so every part of HFAAC gets connected, not just the school and offices.

trainTheTrainer.label: How We Work
trainTheTrainer.heading: Train the trainer
trainTheTrainer.intro: We don't fly in to teach a one-off workshop and leave. Every program is built so a local trainer can carry it forward alone — teaching every week during term time, long after we've gone home.

items.name: Esther & Filder — Crafting Classes
items.text: Our first local teachers, joined in May and July 2025. They lead crochet and handcraft lessons every week.

items.name: Christine — Tailoring Workshop
items.text: Trained by Astrid in 2026, Christine now continues the sewing machine and hand sewing lessons every week as our local trainer.

items.name: Patrick — Carpentry Course
items.text: A foster father at HFAAC with a natural talent for woodwork, Patrick joined as our third local craft teacher in 2025 and has run the carpentry course every week since.

items.name: Philip — Motorbike Riding & Maintenance
items.text: Trained by Jari in 2026, Philip now teaches safe riding and basic maintenance independently, and cares for the motorbike day to day.

items.name: Three Computer Lab trainers
items.text: Prepared in 2026 to run the new computer lab independently, with an eye toward ICDL-equivalent certification down the line.

trainTheTrainer.footerNote: Most of our local trainers are already on HFAAC's official payroll, sponsored by Brian and Brad — a big step toward making every program financially sustainable for the long run.

hfaac.label: Our Partner
hfaac.heading: Hands for an African Child
hfaac.text: Crafting Futures operates in close partnership with **Hands for an African Child (HFAAC)** — a children's village for orphans in Bukomero, Uganda, built up since 2022. HFAAC provides the infrastructure, community connections and local support that make our work possible.
facts: 12 families care for up to 16 orphaned children each, giving them a stable home with their basic needs covered
Its own school on the grounds — Nuri Primary School
A large, self-run farm that helps finance the village
Founded by Americans Brian Matthews and Brad Andersen, but locally led and run, financed through donations and agriculture
